title: Version Migration — agent judgement input
description: The judgement half of a migration report. Written by the agent to .github/.pipeline-context/version-migration/<slug>/migration.json once the build is green on the target runtime, and merged by scripts/render-migration-report.js with the script-generated facts (baseline.json, rounds/round-NN.json, runtime/*.json). Facts about what failed, what was built and what the app answered come from those records — never restate them here. This file carries only what a script cannot know: why each change was needed, which reference rule it came from, and what is left over.

slug.description: The session slug, matching the directory name under .github/.pipeline-context/version-migration/.

title.description: One line naming the jump, e.g. "Spring Boot 3.5.0 to 4.1.1 on Java 21".

summary.description: 3-5 sentences a non-engineer can read: what moved, what had to change in the source because of it, and whether the application still behaves the same. State plainly if anything is unresolved.

reference_pack.description: Reference file this migration followed, e.g. references/spring-boot-3-to-4.md.

name.description: Framework or platform being moved, e.g. Spring Boot.

dependency_changes.description: Every declared coordinate, property or plugin version that changed, including artifacts that were renamed, added or removed.

coordinate.description: groupId:artifactId, a property name, or a plugin id.

from.description: Previous version, or "absent" / the old artifact name when renamed.

reason.description: One sentence citing the reference rule that required it.

code_changes.description: Source changes the framework or language jump forced. One entry per distinct change, not per line.

file.description: Path relative to the project root.

category.description: Short label grouping the change, e.g. "JSON handling", "Health monitoring", "Test wiring".

what.description: One sentence: what changed in this file.

why.description: One sentence: the API/package/behaviour change that forced it.

reference_rule.description: The heading or rule id in the reference pack this came from.

before.description: Short before excerpt — the few lines that changed, not the whole file.

found_in_round.description: Round whose errors surfaced this change, if it was error-driven.

round_notes.description: One entry per build round, in order. Explains what the round's errors meant and what was changed in response. The round's outcome and error counts come from the round record — do not repeat them.

diagnosis.description: What this round's failures actually were, in one short paragraph. For round 0, what the pre-migration build and behaviour established.

changes.description: What was changed in response, one line each. Empty for a round that needed no change.

reference_rules.description: Reference-pack rules applied in this round.

behaviour.description: Verdict on the before/after runtime comparison.

notes.description: For "changed": exactly which probe differs and whether the difference is expected. For "not-compared": why the comparison could not be made.

out_of_scope_changes.description: Changes made or noticed that the migration did NOT require — bug fixes, cleanups, configuration the team wanted anyway. Listing them here keeps the migration story honest; anything here must be presented as separate from the upgrade.

why_separate.description: Why this is not caused by the version jump.

manual_follow_ups.description: What a human must still do: deployment descriptors, infrastructure, credentials, load testing, anything the sandbox could not verify.

residual_risk.description: What could still be wrong even though the build is green and the probes match.
